title: The Lantern at the Bottom of the Mine

r.t: You have been digging down for an hour when your pickaxe breaks through into a small round chamber at the very bottom of the mine. In the middle of the room, a lantern sits on the bare stone, burning with a steady golden light. You never placed it. Nobody else has been down here, and the shaft behind you is silent. The flame leans slightly toward you, as if it has been waiting.

ra.t: The lantern is warm, almost like a living hand. Its light spills across the floor and shows small bare footprints leading from the lantern into a tunnel you never dug. Far down that tunnel, something hums a slow tune, and the flame in your hand hums along. Behind you, the wall you broke through begins to close like a mouth.
ra.c: Smash the lantern on the floor

rb.t: Your voice echoes down the shaft and comes back wrong. A second voice answers, and it sounds exactly like you, calm and friendly. 'Down here,' it says. 'I found something good.' The lantern flame turns to face the tunnel. You hear slow footsteps coming up, matching the rhythm of your own heartbeat.
rb.b: Throw a torch toward the sound

rc.t: You stack cobblestone across the opening and breathe out. For a moment there is only silence. Then the stones begin to tap from the other side, three slow knocks, a pause, three more. A muffled voice whispers through the cracks that it is cold down here and it just wants to go home.
rc.b: Dig a new tunnel around the chamber
rc.c: Run for the ladder and go home

raa.t: You follow the little footprints deeper. The tunnel walls are carved with faces, hundreds of them, all with their eyes closed. Where the lantern light touches them, their eyes slowly open. At the end, a child-sized figure of coal-black stone sits on a chest, humming and holding out both hands for the lantern.
raa.b: Hold the lantern high and refuse

rab.t: You blow out the flame. The dark is total, and in it the humming stops. Something small and cold slips its hand into yours. 'Thank you,' it whispers. 'I couldn't stand the light. Now let's go down together.' Your feet begin to walk, and you cannot make them stop.
rab.a: Fight to pull your hand free
rab.c: Relight the lantern with flint and steel

rac.t: The lantern shatters, and the flame spreads over the stone like liquid gold. It races along the walls, and where it touches, the carved faces wake up screaming. The chamber shakes. Cracks run across the ceiling, and a gap opens in the floor, glowing deep and orange, as if the mine itself is breathing.
rac.b: Climb out through the cracks in the ceiling
rac.c: Stand still and apologize out loud

rba.t: 'I'm here,' you say. The other voice laughs, and a figure wearing your face steps into the lantern's light, holding your own pickaxe. 'I've been waiting a long time to meet you,' it says. 'Let's trade places, just for a while.' The lantern flame turns blue.

rbb.t: Your torch spins into the dark and lights up a long tunnel lined with hanging figures made of coal and string. They sway though there is no wind. In the middle, something tall in a mining helmet turns toward you, holding the lantern. The helmet lamp has no light, only two empty eyes.
rbb.c: Take off your helmet and bow

rbc.t: You climb as fast as you can, but the ladder seems longer than it did on the way down. Each rung you grab is warm and slightly damp. The other voice calls up the shaft in a gentle singsong, getting nearer. Halfway up, the ladder creaks, and a hand wraps around your ankle.
rbc.b: Pull yourself up and shout for help

rca.t: You knock three times. The knocking stops. After a long silence, the stones begin to slide apart, one by one, and a pale hand slips through the gap holding the lantern. 'Thank you for answering,' says the voice, warm and relieved. 'Nobody ever does.' The gap widens.

rcb.t: You dig sideways through the stone, trying to avoid the chamber. The knocking follows you, always one wall away, moving through the rock itself. Your pickaxe breaks into a hollow, and the smell of old candle wax and wet earth pours out. There is a long hall here lined with doors, and every door is knocking.

rcc.t: You run up the ladder without looking back, and the knocking fades to nothing. You hurry home through the dark, lock every door, and light every torch in the house. Just as you sit down to breathe, there is a soft knock at your window, three taps, then three more. A familiar golden glow shows under the curtain.
rcc.c: Slip out the back and run to the village

raaa.t: The figure takes the lantern, and its stone face cracks into a smile. All the carved faces sigh at once, and the tunnel fills with warm light. A door appears behind it, leading straight up to the sunlit surface, and you walk out with the lantern's hum still in your ears. They say a quiet light now burns at the bottom of that mine, and no one who passes it has been lost since.

raab.t: The figure's smile drops. The carved faces all turn toward you, mouths opening in silent screams, and the lantern flame flickers wildly. You run, but every wall you pass reaches out with stone fingers. The last thing you see is the light going out, and the last thing you hear is a small voice saying thank you.

raac.t: Inside the chest lie your own pickaxe, your own armor, and a note in your handwriting: 'You were never the first to find the lantern.' The figure lifts its head, and its face is yours. It takes the lantern gently from your hand and walks up the tunnel wearing your steps, while you realize you are the one left sitting in the dark.

raba.t: You tear your hand away and bolt through the dark, hitting wall after wall. A faint glow shows ahead: the shaft ladder. You climb with the whisper chasing you up every rung, and burst out into the dawn, shaking. Your hand never feels warm again, and sometimes at night it tries to open doors on its own.

rabb.t: You squeeze the little hand back, gently. The cold fades, and the voice laughs softly. 'Nobody ever holds back,' it says. The ground rises under your feet until you step out into the light, and a small stone figure waves from the shaft before crumbling into dust. From then on, you carry a single warm stone in your pocket.

rabc.t: The spark catches, and the flame jumps to life, revealing a small pale face inches from yours, shrieking at the sudden light. It dissolves like smoke. Behind it, the tunnel is full of hundreds of others, all reaching toward the lantern. You hold it high and walk up, followed by a silent crowd of shadows, until the sunrise burns them away.

raca.t: You drop into the glow and land in a warm cavern lit by a sleeping lava lake. A great shape lifts its head, patient and ancient, and the flame from the lantern flows back into its chest. It rumbles a thank-you, and a staircase of obsidian leads you back to the surface. You never find that mine again, but you still dream of the warm dark.

racb.t: You claw up through the falling stone while the screams chase you, and burst out of the ground in a shower of gravel. Behind you the whole hillside folds in on itself, and the mine is gone. In your hand is a single shard of lantern glass, still warm, and on quiet nights it hums.

racc.t: The shaking stops. The faces close their eyes one by one, and the flame pools into a golden puddle at your feet. A voice like wind says it forgives you, but the mine will keep the light now. A staircase of warm stone lifts you gently out of the dark, and you never mine alone again.

rbaa.t: You trade places, and suddenly you are the one standing at the bottom of the mine while your double climbs the ladder, whistling. The lantern warms in your hands. It was never a trap, only a very long shift, and someday another traveler will answer a voice in the dark and take your place.

rbab.t: You swing your pickaxe, and your double swings back with your exact moves. The blades meet in a shower of sparks, and the lantern flares. You realize it can only be beaten by doing something you would never do, so you drop your pickaxe and walk away. The double dissolves like fog, and the ladder is right there.

rbac.t: 'I only wanted company,' it says, and its face softens into a tired smile. It tells you how long it has been down here, waiting for someone to answer. You sit and talk for hours. When you finally leave, it waves from the light, and you promise to visit. Strangely, you do.

rbba.t: You scramble up the ladder as the tall thing follows, rung after rung. At the top you kick the ladder away, and it falls into the dark with a wail. You seal the shaft with obsidian and never mine below sea level again, but some nights you can hear a helmet lamp scraping on the stone beneath your house.

rbbb.t: The torches pile at its feet and set the coal figures alight. The whole tunnel erupts in warm light, and the tall thing lets out a long sigh of relief. It drops the lantern, and the helmet clatters to the ground, empty. A passage opens to the surface, and a small pickaxe lies waiting on the stone as a gift.

rbbc.t: You take off your helmet and bow. The tall thing tilts its head, then removes its own helmet and places it on yours. Suddenly you can see every tunnel in the mountain, every vein of ore, every hidden room. You are the new keeper of the mine, and the lantern follows you wherever you walk.

rbca.t: You kick hard, and the hand lets go with a splash of dark water. You haul yourself over the lip and slam a block of stone across the shaft. In the silence you hear a soft laugh, and a single rung from the ladder lies at your feet, wet and warm. You keep it as a warning.

rbcb.t: Your shout echoes across the whole valley, and lanterns light up in a dozen distant windows. The hand lets go as villagers rush to the shaft with torches, and the thing below hisses and retreats. You are pulled out, safe, to discover your hair has turned white.

rbcc.t: You look down. The face looking up at you is your own, smiling, wearing a lantern like a crown. It says, very gently, 'Thanks for the light,' and lets go. You fall forever, or at least it feels like it, and wake on the surface at dawn with the lantern in your hand, burning exactly as it was.

rcaa.t: You take the lantern, and the hand lets go. The wall seals itself, and the pale voice whispers a quiet goodbye before fading. The lantern burns steadily, and in its light you see that the whole tunnel ahead is lined with torches, all lit. It was never a monster, only lonely, and you leave with a friend's light.

rcab.t: You slam the stone back, and a scream rattles the mine. The lantern light under the stones turns red, and the wall pulses like a heart. You run up the ladder with the knocking chasing you, and the whole mountain shudders behind. By morning the shaft is filled with solid stone, and something is knocking in your cellar.

rcac.t: 'I'm the one who dug this mine,' says the voice. 'I forgot to leave.' The lantern flame softens, and in its light you glimpse an old miner sitting calmly in the dark. He asks you to bury his helmet in the sun, and when you do, the mine falls quiet forever, and the lantern never needs lighting again.

rcba.t: You open the nearest door and find a tiny room with a bed, a table, and a lantern just like yours, burning gently. A voice says, 'Welcome home,' and the door closes behind you. You sleep, and when you wake there is no door at all, only warm stone and a lantern, and the knocking has become your own heartbeat.

rcbb.t: You block the hole with every block you have and curl up in the corner, shaking. The knocking slows, then stops, and a single note of soft humming begins, calm as a lullaby. By dawn you have fallen asleep, and when you wake the mine is just a mine, with a small lantern set neatly beside you.

rcbc.t: You run, and every door slams open as you pass, flooding the hall with golden light. At the far end is the ladder, and above it the sky. You climb, laughing and panting, and the lights behind you go out one by one like a thousand tiny goodbyes.

rcca.t: You open the door. A small stone figure stands on your step, holding the lantern out with both hands, its face a crooked smile. It sets the lantern on your table, bows, and walks back into the night. The lantern never goes out, and your house is never cold again.

rccb.t: You blow out the torches and sit in the dark, listening. The knocking stops. Then a soft humming starts in the corner of the room, and something small sits down beside you. In the morning there is nothing there except a warm patch on the floor, and the feeling that you are no longer alone.

rccc.t: You run for the village and bang on every door, but nobody wakes. When you turn around, the golden glow has followed you down the road and fills the whole street. The doors open at last, and a crowd of sleepwalkers steps out, each carrying a lantern, and calls you by name.
